title: Certificates of Deposit: Grounds for Reversing an Early Withdrawal Penalty
content:
A penalty charged on one of the bank's Certificates of Deposit can be credited back to the certificate at Piedmont Crescent Bank, but only on defined grounds. This page lists those grounds, the form a reversal takes, and its limits.

## Form of a reversal

A penalty is reversed in its entirety or not at all; a partial reversal does not exist. The reversal is one credit entry on the certificate that identifies the penalty entry it cancels, and it is recorded with one of two adjustment reasons.

## Reason: bank error

A penalty is reversed for bank error when it was charged in breach of the certificate terms, namely where it was charged:

- on a penalty-free withdrawal from a no-penalty certificate made after the waiting days had passed;
- on a withdrawal of interest already credited;
- using a number of penalty days, or a rate, that differs from what the terms prescribe;
- on a penalty basis larger than the principal the withdrawal actually removed.

The earlier listing of a penalty charged on a withdrawal made in the grace period as, without more, a bank-error ground is **no longer in force**; penalties on grace-period withdrawals are now reversed under the current basis for them.

## Reason: death waiver

A penalty is reversed under the death waiver when the bank's estate services confirm that the withdrawal came after the owner's death or after a court adjudicated the owner incompetent.

## Limits

- **Once only.** A penalty that already has a reversal entry pointing to it is never reversed again. The bank's ledger for that penalty is the evidence.
- **No goodwill reversals.** A penalty that was charged correctly is not reversed as a courtesy under these rules.

## Decision table (hypothetical penalties)

| Penalty found on the certificate | Already reversed? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Charged on a full withdrawal of an 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate made after its waiting days | No | Reverse in full, bank error |
| Charged on a withdrawal of interest that had already been credited | No | Reverse in full, bank error |
| Charged on the whole balance although only part of it was withdrawn | No | Reverse in full, bank error |
| Charged correctly; the owner asks for a courtesy refund | No | Not reversed |
| Any penalty qualifying above | Yes | Not reversed again |
| Charged on a withdrawal that estate services confirm followed the owner's death | No | Reverse in full, death waiver |
